request.spec:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added review assignment and three of the four tests pass, including the main "review assignment" test. "Review assignment scenario 1" still fails, at `acceptance.spec.ts:375`: `rate-current-B` shows `n/a` where the test expects `7.50`. That check is about rates, not review assignment, and I believe it's caused by today's date rather than by my change. I didn't prove that by running the test without my change, and I didn't change anything to make it pass.

**Why scenario 1 fails:** the scenario creates a parent sheet (`<sheet>-p`) and sets grade B to 7.50 there, but never sets that sheet's "today". A new sheet's today comes from the real clock (`SheetRepository.java:23`), so that rate starts on 2026-11-12. The test then views the child sheet as of 2026-03-20, before the parent's rate begins, so B has no rate. The expected `7.50` only holds if the test runs on or before 2026-03-20. Making it pass would mean changing how a new sheet's today defaults, which is outside this change request, so I left it alone.

**What I changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V119__claim_review_user.sql`, adds a `review_user` column to the claim table and to the claim history table. The claim store reads it, keeps it in history and in as-of views, and saves an assignment only while the claim is still in REVIEW.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/review-assign`. It refuses a viewer, a blank user, a claim not in REVIEW, and anyone who isn't a steward; someone a steward has delegated to counts as a steward. A refusal writes nothing. On success it writes `REVIEW_ASSIGNED … person= amount= date= user=<user>`, and the existing audit service adds `for=<steward>` when the action was delegated. Each claim the screen receives now includes the assigned user.
- **Front end:**
  - Each claim row now has an entry (`claim-review-user`), an "Assign review" button (`claim-review-assign`) and the assigned user (`claim-review-assigned`).
  - A refusal shows the existing `claim-error`, which clears when you type in the entry or take the next action.
  - The header shows `my-reviews-count`: how many REVIEW claims are assigned to the signed-in user.
- The assigned user stays on a claim after it leaves REVIEW, as the test expects, but it no longer counts toward anyone's header count.
